known_issues: Default READY and an in-budget semantic source do not guarantee optional native admission. The inherited catalog profile requires both PDF /ID entries to parse as 32-character TextStringObject values; the unchanged renderer's raw HTML SHA-256 identifier can instead parse as ByteStringObject. Such a generated candidate is refused without rewriting the identifier, changing the source or retrying.
This is an explicit private candidate entrypoint for the existing semantic-section/en-US source. It does not activate typed PDF, assets, links, a new report family or scientific interpretation.
The default protocol-1 renderer and 32-page/8-MiB candidate-readiness route remain unchanged. Optional protocol 2 admits at most 64 pages and 16 MiB, conditional on every unchanged inner limit.

The same pinned renderer produces the whole PDF; strict physical page discovery occurs in its bounded child without rewriting or padding the PDF. The native source inspector independently rechecks the full artifact and page plan.

A finite 16-MiB admission ceiling does not establish authentic source generation above 8 MiB. Natural long-source tests qualify page integration only; complete larger-than-32-page AND larger-than-8-MiB final generation remains unqualified.

The 330-second post-admission check is an acceptance deadline. Render and native stages retain separate child lifetime and cleanup controls. Parent work, spawning and syscalls are not preempted; whole-graph CPU, RSS, scratch, descriptor and descendant budgets remain unqualified.

Two outer stages do not mean two native launches. The existing native inspector owns its own launch scope; this coordinator does not nest a new scope or provide retry, resume or durable checkpoint inputs.

Retained sealed results are revalidated before metadata or private candidate bytes are exposed. Source and job agreement is unsigned consistency, not authenticated execution, clinical authority or authorization to release.
Persistent source mutation is rejected through bounded captured/original comparisons. Concurrent mutate-and-restore behavior remains unsupported.

Native text, graph and same-font explicit-width checks do not establish visible glyphs, scientific equivalence, finding completeness, semantic accessibility, PDF/UA conformance, frozen visual baselines or complete final-report QA.
